name: Measure AA Restoration Authority Grants
summary: Annual competitive grant round funding shoreline habitat restoration, flood management and public access projects around San Francisco Bay, with priority for projects benefiting disadvantaged communities and Tribes.

steps: Review by at least three experts

eligibility.rule: Project is along the listed Bay shorelines and outside the Delta Primary Zone
Project is shoreline habitat work, or flood management or public access that is part of one
Not off-site mitigation such as mitigation banks or in-lieu fees
Construction project has completed CEQA analysis
Project will be ready to use Authority funds within 12 months of the application due date
An acquisition is transacted with a willing seller

documents: Tribal leadership letter, if a Tribe or Tribal organization is involved
Landowner letter, if the applicant is not the landowner

geography.quote: Habitat projects that aim to restore, protect, or enhance natural habitats on the shoreline in the San Francisco Bay Area

access.quote: More information on project eligibility, eligible grantees, and prioritization criteria can be found in the Request for Proposals.

effort.quote: It is recommended that all applicants complete a Pre-Application and request a consultation with Authority staff by September 4, 2026.
Grant Round Full Applications Due October 5, 2026 by midnight
The Authority staff will screen grant applications to ensure that:
Complete applications that have passed the screening process will be reviewed and evaluated by a minimum of three professionals with relevant expertise in the Authority's program areas

eligibility.quote: Projects must also be along the shorelines of San Francisco Bay, San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait, Suisun Bay, and most of the Northern Contra Costa County Shoreline (not including the Delta Primary Zone - see Appendix C)

Habitat projects that aim to restore, protect, or enhance natural habitats on the shoreline in the San Francisco Bay Area; Flood management projects that are part of habitat projects; or Public access projects that will provide or improve access or recreational amenities that are part of habitat projects.

The Authority will not fund project that are not carried out on-site as part of the restoration project (e.g., mitigation through private mitigation banks, in-lieu fees, or other off-site mitigation actions).
The Authority will only authorize funding for construction projects that have completed CEQA analysis.
The project will be ready to use Authority funds within 12 months of the application due date.

after_award.quote: Grantees must submit invoices and progress reports regularly, and at least quarterly.

documents.quote: SFBRA Cover Sheet (PDF Format) Project description section I Preliminary budget section II Prioritization criteria section III SFBRA Budget Template (Excel Format) Project maps and design plans (in one pdf file, 10 MB maximum size) Project photos (in jpg format)

If a Tribe or Tribal organization has confirmed their interest in the project, a letter from their leadership confirming their involvement If you are not the landowner, a letter from the landowner confirming their willingness to host the project Support letters from community-based organizations, local jurisdictions, partners, and/or other community representatives
If you are not the landowner, a letter from the landowner confirming their willingness to host the project
